experiment: P3o-N observable resolution-aware abstention for compound MFT target count
research_question: When the same sparse-peak ordinal MFT-count predictor is held fixed, does an observable peak-resolution score provide lower matched-coverage count risk than ordinary ordinal-confidence gating on fresh compound identities?

prior_boundary.P3oM: sparse peak tokenization improved point MAE over a fixed-bin control but failed the 3/3 low-count Pearson gate; P3o-M identities, peak rule, token count and loss are forbidden for selection
prior_boundary.mechanism_change: decision reliability, not a change to the point estimator: C0 and C1 share exactly the same trained sparse-peak ordinal checkpoint and point predictions
forbidden: P3o-M identities for calibration or tuning

roles.gate_calibration: selection only; exactly top 80 percent per score, deterministic stable rank
roles.development: all 33 identities per combination; read once after method freeze

shared_point_estimator.input: P3o-M frozen four-channel sparse local-peak tokens, 16 tokens

decision_controls.C0_ordinal_confidence: maximum normalized mass induced by monotone cumulative ordinal probabilities
decision_controls.C1_resolution_aware: C0 confidence times mean contrast of the top predicted-count local peaks times min(1, minimum selected-peak position gap / 0.04); one predicted peak uses gap factor one

stop_rule: If any promotion gate fails, stop P3o-N. Do not tune the resolution formula, gap scale, target coverage, token rule, network, loss, training, or calibration on 1720M/1730M. Do not generate confirmation identities or attach to the full system.
next_if_pass: Freeze scores, thresholds, checkpoints and code; evaluate two untouched identity confirmations using the same 80 percent selection-role threshold rule before any predicted-label-gated MFT-only attachment.
